questions.q: What does Black Beauty say could have prevented much of the horses' trouble in London?
questions.evidence: much of it might have been prevented by a little common sense

questions.q: Which old friend did the little gray pony remind Black Beauty of?
questions.evidence: so much like Merrylegs that if I had not been in harness I should have neighed to him

questions.q: What condition was the butcher's horse in when the cart dashed up?
choices: Hot and worn out, its sides heaving
Fresh and calm after a short trot
Limping badly from a lost shoe
Cool and dry, as if just out of the stable
questions.evidence: The horse was hot and much exhausted

questions.q: Why was the butcher angry with the lad?
choices: He drove it too hard, and had ruined the last horse
He was late home for his dinner again
He had lost the basket of meat on the way
He had given meat away to his friends for free
questions.evidence: You ruined the last horse and broke his wind

questions.q: Who did the butcher's son blame for all the hurry?
choices: Customers who did not order their meat in time
The horse, for being lazy and slow on the hills
The police, for stopping him in the street
His mother, for sending him out so late
questions.evidence: If the gentry would think of what they want, and order their meat the day before

questions.q: The coster-boy's pony was "the cheerfullest and pluckiest little thing." What does "pluckiest" mean?
questions.evidence: the cheerfullest and pluckiest little thing I ever saw
